text.p: Following are the main stories in Tuesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
All papers lead with Singapore Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew's statement that he would ask a local court to delete from the record his criticism of a neighbouring Malaysian state.
-- Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad told Malaysian state governments to forgo early profits from large-scale industries by giving them a chance to first establish their businesses.

-- Works Minister Samy Vellu warned that contractors at the new Kuala Lumpur airport must complete their projects on schedule or face penalties. He was earlier briefed that there were delays in parts of the project.
-- Development of high-tech city Cyberjaya is being speeded up due to overwhelming response, said Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim.
-- The Malaysian Cabinet has banned the cloning of humans but will allow animal cloning for scientific purposes, said Health Minister Chua Jui Meng.
